agent was given its name, signature, neighboring names and comments — never
its body — and wrote down what it expected to find. Then it opened the file.

there.

`read at` is a hash of the body as it was when the reading was made. When it
stops matching the code, the reading is marked STALE and goes back in the
queue.

## crates/dvda-demuxer/src/tui/dvda/cppm.rs

### the file itself
- spec 3 · read at `714db952c823` · commit `1681528` · read by claude-sonnet-5 · via claude · when 2026-08-20T04:58:19Z · by ross@rossturk.com · cold reading · reading 7 of its run · priming: CLAUDE.md excluded
- expected: This file implements CPPM (DVD-Audio copy-protection) detection: since actual CPPM decryption isn't implemented, it infers protection status heuristically by checking whether a Media Key Block (MKB) is present on the disc and then probing whether an Audio Object (AOB) file's sectors actually contain readable/valid MPEG-PS audio data. If MKB is present but the probed AOB data isn't readable, it flags the disc as CPPM-protected (blocking further processing); if the AOB data is readable despite MKB presence, it assumes no active protection. It also supports an "assume decrypted" override to bypass the probe/blocking, and includes in-memory mock DvdaFile/DvdaVolume test fixtures plus a substantial test suite covering these detection paths.
- found: refine_copy_protection_from_aob_probe decides CPPM status: if assume_decrypted override is set, disables blocking; else if MKB absent, no-op; else probes the first backed AOB's first sector for a valid MPEG-PS pack header and readable DVD-Audio private-stream-1 substream (via manual PES packet walking and a substream sub-header byte check for 0xA0/0xA1), setting cppm_detected true only when MKB is present and the probe fails to find readable audio data. Includes in-memory test volume/file mocks and tests for each branch.
- predicted: most · documented: none · derivable: yes · legible: not judged · trap: no
